00688.regimen_rationale: Atezolizumab blocks PD-L1 signalling; albumin-bound paclitaxel is a microtubule-directed cytotoxic drug. Intended to control eligible advanced TNBC, not a curative early-breast regimen.
00688.biomarker: Ventana SP142 tumour-infiltrating immune-cell score, with stained immune-cell area at least 1% of tumour area. This is neither CPS nor tumour-cell percentage.
00688.status: NCCP00688 v2a and current EMA TNBC indication remain available in Ireland/EU source documents checked on this date; prior metastatic chemotherapy is excluded by the indication. Confirm individual clinical eligibility and approval.

studies.population: 902 patients with untreated unresectable locally advanced/metastatic TNBC; 451 per arm; PD-L1 IC+ subgroup 185 versus 184.
studies.comparison: Atezolizumab 840 mg Days 1/15 plus nab-paclitaxel 100 mg/m² Days 1/8/15 every 28 days versus placebo plus the same nab-paclitaxel.

endpoints.endpoint: Investigator PFS in PD-L1 IC+ subgroup

limitations: PFS and OS are different endpoints. Group medians are not an individual prognosis or guaranteed months gained.
Evidence depends on the exact nab-paclitaxel combination and biomarker population; no early-breast extrapolation.

studies.population: Same randomised trial, final OS analysis; median follow-up 18.8 months overall.

endpoints.inference: Exploratory/descriptive; formal testing was prevented by the prespecified hierarchy after nonsignificant ITT OS.

limitations: Do not describe the subgroup OS estimate as a formally proven survival advantage.
Do not mix these final OS estimates with earlier interim values or use the median difference as an individual survival promise.

studies.population: 651 patients with advanced TNBC; 45% PD-L1 positive. A different chemotherapy formulation: solvent-based paclitaxel.
limitations: Atezolizumab plus solvent-based paclitaxel did not improve PFS or OS. This trial does not support substituting solvent paclitaxel in NCCP00688.

00688.consent_benefit_text: In the biomarker-selected trial group, the combination delayed cancer progression compared with nab-paclitaxel alone. Survival results in that subgroup were exploratory. Discuss likely disease control, symptoms and adverse effects for the individual situation.
safety_priorities: Immune inflammation involving bowel, lung, liver, kidney, hormones, skin, heart or nervous system, including delayed events
No routine solvent-paclitaxel steroid premedication is copied to nab-paclitaxel

00738.regimen_rationale: Bevacizumab targets VEGF-mediated angiogenesis; paclitaxel interferes with microtubules. Intended for metastatic disease control under the agreed treatment plan.
00738.status: NCCP00738 v3 lists triple-negative or HER2-negative metastatic breast cancer. EMA licenses first-line metastatic breast cancer with paclitaxel; establish line of treatment and local approval.

studies.population: 722 patients receiving initial chemotherapy for metastatic breast cancer; predominantly HER2-negative, not a TNBC-only trial.
studies.comparison: Paclitaxel 90 mg/m² Days 1/8/15 every 28 days with or without bevacizumab 10 mg/kg Days 1/15.
limitations: NCCP00738 uses paclitaxel 80 mg/m²; E2100 tested 90 mg/m². Label this dose mismatch explicitly.
No demonstrated OS advantage; do not convert PFS improvement into a survival claim.
The original publication estimates are retained together; EMA presents different assessment/reanalysis values and they must not be blended.
Not TNBC-only evidence and not an individual prognosis.

00738.consent_benefit_text: A related trial showed longer time before progression and more tumour responses with bevacizumab plus paclitaxel, but did not show a significant survival improvement. Its paclitaxel dose was 90 mg/m²; this NCCP schedule uses 80 mg/m².
safety_priorities: Paclitaxel low counts, infection, neuropathy and infusion reactions
Bevacizumab hypertension, urine protein loss, bleeding/clots, wound-healing problems and uncommon bowel perforation
Surgery timing and healed wounds must be reviewed; bevacizumab is held or stopped rather than dose-reduced
